title: What a runway estimate hides about a founder’s cash timing

intent.question: How does a fixed monthly cash-burn assumption change a runway estimate?
intent.readerDecision: Identify which timing and cost assumptions need checking before relying on a simple runway figure.
intent.uniqueValue: A reproducible example distinguishes cash available, net cash use and break-even assumptions, then explains why an accounting profit does not establish a cash balance.

sources.name: US Small Business Administration: Plan your business
sources.purpose: Identify the official startup-cost and planning guidance relevant to defining the scenario; verify the exact supporting sections before citation.

methodology.plan: Run labeled cash scenarios through the versioned cash-runway calculator. Explain gross spending versus net cash burn, compare alternative monthly assumptions, and identify receivable timing, one-time costs and financing events that a constant-burn model omits.
assumptions: Cash balance and monthly revenue and spending figures are hypothetical and use consistent units.
The simple comparison holds the chosen monthly cash flows constant.
limitations: A calculation based on constant monthly burn is not a forecast of liquidity or solvency.
Seasonality, payment delays, liabilities and financing conditions require separate analysis.

disclaimer: Educational research planning only. This draft does not provide accounting, lending, insolvency or financial advice, and its illustrative cash figures must not be used as operating targets.

contextualLinks.reason: Would connect the explanation to a reproducible input model after the article and link have received editorial approval.
